subject: Exchange of value of x & y

messages.author: ccd78931d1fcec11
messages.subject: Exchange of value of x & y
parts:
Hi Chris,

I read your paper several weeks ago and have been fitting exploring the ctmm package with my fox tracking data. 

However, I have been bothered by some quite weird issues ----

The first is the weirdest one. I have data collected from over 20 foxes, and the latitudinal range of some them are larger than their longitudinal range (when mapped out its more like a portrait look), while naturally the rest of them are more like a landscape look. 
However, when I used the 'as.telemetry' function to turn these 'portrait look' data in to telemetry data and plotted them out, no matter before or after doing the home range estimation, the out put maps were all wrong. Specifically, they were the exact right map but after diagonal and vertical reflection. However, all the landscape look datasets are all good. I tried this many times, even on my colleagues' computer, and the results were all the same.

The second question was more theoretical, I tried the weighted function and was quite intrigued by it. The question is, what will happen if I just use this function to all the datasets, even in the ones that are not necessary for it? Overfitting? 

Lastly, how do I export the final home range as shape file? I read this part in the R document, but just couldn't get the code right. 

Thanks so much!

(The first picture is what the map should look like, and the second one is the one created by ctmm. but if the map is landscape look initially, there will be no problem.)

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Exchange of value of x & y
parts:
Hi,

You can use the compass() command to see which direction is north in the current projection. See the example in in the projection() help file. The default projection does not preserve north being up.

Weighted AKDE can be used when you don't need it and it won't make for a substantial difference in that case. The calculation will just take longer.

Export options are documented in ?export
writeVector() is probably what you want.

Best,
Chris
